claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The proposed computational method uses machine-learning interatomic potentials.
The proposed method can accurately predict the lattice heat-transport contribution in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed method can accurately predict the electronic heat-transport contribution in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed method will outperform earlier heat-transport approaches.
Capturing atomic-scale complexity is responsible for the proposed method's improved performance.
Capturing defect effects is responsible for the proposed method's improved performance.
The method is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing defects or impurities such as 1 wt.% oxygen.
The method is applicable below 200 K.
The method is applicable from 300 to 1200 K.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials capture local lattice distortion.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials capture dislocation motion.
Capturing local lattice distortion and dislocation motion improves prediction of both lattice and electronic heat transport.
Application of the proposed computational method may correspond to an increase in total conductivity.
Measured total conductivity from 300 to 1200 K is 10–17 W/(K m).
Temperatures above 1200 K are outside the proposed applicability boundary.
Temperatures below 200 K constitute an applicability limit.
A deviation of more than 20% between predicted and measured total conductivity falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Below 200 K is listed both as an intended operating condition and as a temperature limit, leaving it unclear whether this range is inside or outside applicability.
The boundary states specific temperature limits, while the uncertainty field says the temperature limits remain quantitatively uncertain.

The hypothesis requires separate prediction of lattice and electronic contributions, but the numerical falsification rule tests only their combined total conductivity; compensating component errors could therefore pass the stated test.
